records.gloss: For the director, with stringed instruments. A psalm of Asaph, a song.
pieces: For the music director. With stringed instruments. A psalm of Asaph. A song.

L.1: For the director: with stringed instruments. A psalm of Asaph, a song.

R.1: For the leader of the music. To be played on stringed instruments. A song of Asaph.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, probably the leader of the temple music.

decisions.choice: stringed instruments: to be accompanied on strings
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, the word (neginot) is used for music played on strings.

decisions.choice: Asaph: a leader of the temple singers
decisions.reason: Asaph was a Levite whom David appointed to lead the singing before the ark (1 Chronicles 16:5-7); his family carried on the work (1 Chronicles 25:1-2). Psalms 50 and 73-83 bear his name.

decisions.choice: song
decisions.reason: As in 3:1, Readable says what a psalm is.

records.heading: God breaks the weapons at Zion

records.source: נוֹדָ֣ע בִּֽיהוּדָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֑ים בְּ֝יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל גָּד֥וֹל שְׁמֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Known in Judah [is] God; in Israel great [is] his name.
pieces: God has made {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} known in Judah; \q {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name stands high in Israel.

L.2: God [is] known in Judah; \q in Israel {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name [is] great.

R.2: The people of Judah know who God is. \q In Israel everyone honors {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.

decisions.choice: a song of Zion
decisions.reason: Like Psalms 46, 48 and 87, this psalm celebrates Zion, Jerusalem, as the place where God lives and from which he breaks the power of the armies that come against it (verses 4-7). Its picture of an army struck down in its sleep recalls the night the Assyrian army besieging Jerusalem was struck (Isaiah 37:36), and the ancient Greek translation adds "concerning the Assyrian" to the title.

decisions.choice: known: made known by what he has done
decisions.reason: The form (noda') means "is known" or "has made himself known": God is known in Judah because he has acted there (9:17).

decisions.choice: his name: his fame, God as he is known
decisions.reason: A great name is a great reputation; God's name stands for God himself as people know him (8:2).

records.gloss: And was in Salem his lair, and his den in Zion.
pieces: His lair is set in Salem, \q {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} den in Zion.

L.3: And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} lair was in Salem, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} den in Zion.

R.3: He has made Jerusalem {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} home. \q Like a lion in its den, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives on Mount Zion.

decisions.choice: Salem: Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Salem is an old name for Jerusalem; Melchizedek was king of Salem (Genesis 14:18). It stands in parallel with Zion, the hill of the city where the temple stood.

decisions.choice: lair and den: the shelter of a lion
decisions.reason: The two words (sok, me'onah) can mean a hut or a dwelling, but both are used of a lion's lair (10:9; Jeremiah 25:38; Job 38:40). God is pictured as a lion who rises from his den to defend his city.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem; Like a lion in its den
decisions.reason: Readable names the city (m1) and makes the picture a comparison (m2).

records.source: שָׁ֭מָּה שִׁבַּ֣ר רִשְׁפֵי־קָ֑שֶׁת מָגֵ֬ן וְחֶ֖רֶב וּמִלְחָמָ֣ה סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: There he broke [the] flames of [the] bow, shield and sword and battle. Selah.
pieces: There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shattered the fiery shafts of the bow, \q shield and sword and all the gear of battle. Selah

L.4: There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke the flames of the bow, \q shield and sword and battle. Selah

R.4: There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke the enemy's burning arrows, \q their shields and swords, and everything they used to fight. Selah

decisions.choice: flames of the bow: arrows
decisions.reason: The word (reshef) means a flame or flash. "Flames of the bow" are arrows, flashing as they fly, or arrows set alight.

decisions.choice: battle: the weapons of battle
decisions.reason: After shield and sword, "battle" stands for every weapon of war (Hosea 2, where God breaks bow, sword and battle). God ends the war by breaking the weapons (46:10).

decisions.choice: the enemy's
decisions.reason: Readable names whose weapons were broken, the armies that came against the city.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

records.gloss: Shining [are] you, majestic, more than [the] mountains of prey.
pieces: You shine with light, \q in greater splendor than the mountains of prey.

L.5: Shining [are] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, majestic, \q more than the mountains of prey.

R.5: You shine with glory! \q You are more splendid than the mountains where wild beasts hunt.

decisions.choice: shining: full of light
decisions.reason: The form (na'or) means lit up or radiant: God appears in blazing light, like the light in which he came from Sinai (Deuteronomy 33:2).

decisions.choice: mountains of prey: where beasts of prey hunt
alternatives: returning from the mountains with the spoil
decisions.reason: The phrase continues the lion picture of verse 3. It may mean the mountains where beasts of prey live, or the hills from which God returns with the spoil of the beaten army (verse 6). Either way God is greater than all that is fierce and strong.

decisions.choice: of prey
alternatives: the everlasting mountains (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation reads "everlasting mountains", from a word that looks much like "prey" in the Hebrew script. The words follow the Hebrew text.

records.source: אֶשְׁתּוֹלְל֨וּ׀אַבִּ֣ירֵי לֵ֭ב נָמ֣וּ שְׁנָתָ֑ם וְלֹא־מָצְא֖וּ כָל־אַנְשֵׁי־חַ֣יִל יְדֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: They were plundered, [the] mighty of heart; they slept their sleep, and not found all [the] men of strength their hands.
pieces: The brave were stripped bare; they dropped into their final sleep, \q and not one of the warriors could find a hand to raise.

L.6: The mighty of heart were plundered; they slept their sleep, \q and none of the men of strength found their hands.

R.6: The proud soldiers were robbed of all they had. They fell asleep and never woke up. \q Not one of those strong fighters could even lift a hand.

decisions.choice: slept their sleep: died
decisions.reason: Sleep here is the sleep of death, as in 13:4 and Jeremiah 51:39, 57. The army that came to plunder is plundered.

decisions.choice: did not find their hands: were helpless
decisions.reason: Not finding one's hands means having no strength to use them. The strong men could do nothing.

decisions.choice: final sleep (B); never woke up (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make plain that the sleep is death (m1).

records.source: מִ֭גַּעֲרָ֣תְךָ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֑ב נִ֝רְדָּ֗ם וְרֶ֣כֶב וָסֽוּס׃
records.gloss: From your rebuke, God of Jacob, [was] sleeping both chariot and horse.
pieces: When {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rebuked them, God of Jacob, \q chariot and horse sank into a stupor.

L.7: At {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rebuke, God of Jacob, \q both chariot and horse [were] in deep sleep.

R.7: God of Jacob, when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} shouted at them, \q their chariots and horses lay still as if dead.

decisions.choice: rebuke: God's battle cry
decisions.reason: God's rebuke (ge'arah) is the angry shout that drives back enemies and even the sea (18:16; 104:7). One word from him stops an army.

decisions.choice: sleeping: in a deep, deathlike sleep
decisions.reason: The verb (radam) is used of a heavy sleep from which one does not easily wake (Judges 4:21; Daniel 10:9).

decisions.choice: chariot and horse: as at the Red Sea
decisions.reason: The words recall God's victory over Pharaoh's chariots and horses at the sea (Exodus 14:23; 15:1, 21).

records.source: אַתָּ֤ה׀נ֥וֹרָא אַ֗תָּה וּמִֽי־יַעֲמֹ֥ד לְפָנֶ֗יךָ מֵאָ֥ז אַפֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: You — fearsome [are] you, and who will stand before you from [the] time of your anger?
pieces: You, yes, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are to be feared! \q When {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger blazes, \q who can hold out in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} presence?

L.8: You — {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] fearsome! \q And who will stand before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} \q from the moment of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger?

R.8: You are the one everyone should fear! \q When {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are angry, no one can stand up to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: you, you: strongly emphatic
decisions.reason: The pronoun is said twice for emphasis: God and no one else is to be feared.

decisions.choice: from the time of your anger: as soon as you are angry
decisions.reason: The words (me'az 'appekha) mean "from then of your anger", that is, once your anger is roused no one can stand (Nahum 1, where no one stands before his fury).

decisions.choice: no one can stand up to you
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies.

records.source: מִ֭שָּׁמַיִם הִשְׁמַ֣עְתָּ דִּ֑ין אֶ֖רֶץ יָֽרְאָ֣ה וְשָׁקָֽטָה׃
records.gloss: From heaven you made heard judgment; [the] earth feared and was quiet,
pieces: From heaven {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} announced {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} verdict; \q the earth was afraid and fell silent,

L.9: From heaven {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made judgment heard; \q [the] earth feared and was still,

R.9: You announced {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sentence from heaven. \q The whole earth was afraid and became silent.

decisions.choice: judgment: a verdict
decisions.reason: The word (din) is the decision of a judge. God pronounces his verdict from heaven, and the whole earth hears it.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: Verse 10 tells when this happened ("when God rose"), so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.gloss: when arose for judgment God to save all [the] humble of [the] earth. Selah.
pieces: when God stood up to give judgment \q and to rescue all the lowly on earth. Selah

L.10: when God arose for judgment, \q to save all the humble of the earth. Selah

R.10: That happened when God stood up to judge \q and to save all the people on earth who were poor and crushed. Selah

decisions.choice: the humble: the poor and oppressed
decisions.reason: The word ('anavim) means people who are low, poor and oppressed, and who depend on God (9:19; 37:11). God's judgment is their rescue.

decisions.choice: the earth
decisions.reason: The word ('erets) can mean the whole earth or the land of Israel. After verse 9 it is taken as the earth.

decisions.choice: That happened
decisions.reason: Readable begins a new sentence, so it links it to verse 9.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

records.source: כִּֽי־חֲמַ֣ת אָדָ֣ם תּוֹדֶ֑ךָּ שְׁאֵרִ֖ית חֵמֹ֣ת תַּחְגֹּֽר׃
records.gloss: For [the] wrath of humankind will praise you; [the] remainder of wraths you will gird on.
pieces: Even human fury will end in praise for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q what is left of it {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will tie on like a belt.

L.11: For the wrath of humankind will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q the remnant of wrath {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will gird on.

R.11: Even when people rage against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, it ends in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} praise. \q You will take whatever anger is left and wear it like a belt.

decisions.choice: the wrath of humankind will praise you: human rage ends by bringing God praise
alternatives: your wrath against humankind brings you praise
decisions.reason: The rage of the nations against God's people only gives God an occasion to show his power, so in the end it brings him praise. The words can also mean God's anger against people.

decisions.choice: the remainder of wraths you will gird on
alternatives: you will restrain the rest of their rage
the survivors of wrath will keep a feast to you (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: This line is hard. "Gird" means to put on as a belt: God wears the last of the fury as a trophy, or girds himself with his own anger. Some take the verb as "restrain". The ancient Greek translation reads "the remnant of wrath will keep a feast to you".

decisions.choice: people rage against you
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain whose anger is meant (m1).

records.source: נִֽדֲר֣וּ וְשַׁלְּמוּ֮ לַיהוָ֪ה אֱֽלֹהֵ֫יכֶ֥ם כָּל־סְבִיבָ֑יו יוֹבִ֥ילוּ שַׁ֝֗י לַמּוֹרָֽא׃
records.gloss: Vow and pay to YHWH your God; all [those] around him, let them bring a gift to the Fearsome [One].
pieces: Vow to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and keep what you vow; \q let all who surround {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} \q bring tribute to the One who inspires fear.

L.12: Vow and pay [your vows] to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God; \q let all who are around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} \q bring a gift to the Fearsome One.

R.12: Make promises to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and then keep them. \q Let all the nations around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} \q bring gifts to the God everyone must fear.

decisions.choice: vow and pay: promise an offering and give it
decisions.reason: A vow was a promise to give God an offering, often made in trouble and paid after rescue (22:26; 50:14). Those God has saved are to keep their promises.

decisions.choice: all around him: the surrounding peoples
decisions.reason: "All around him" may be the nations surrounding Israel, who bring tribute to the God who broke the armies (68:30), or the people standing around him in worship.

decisions.choice: the Fearsome One: a title of God
decisions.reason: The word (mora') means fear or what is feared; here it names God himself, the one who is to be feared (verse 8).

decisions.choice: all the nations around him
decisions.reason: Readable follows the likelier sense (m2).

records.gloss: He cuts off [the] spirit of rulers; fearsome to [the] kings of [the] earth.
pieces: He cuts short the breath of princes; \q the kings of the earth stand in fear of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.13: He cuts off the spirit of rulers; \q [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is] fearsome to the kings of the earth.

R.13: He humbles proud rulers. \q The kings of the earth are afraid of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: cuts off: harvests, cuts down
decisions.reason: The verb (batsar) is used for cutting off grapes at the harvest. God cuts rulers down as easily as grapes are picked.

decisions.choice: spirit: pride, or the breath of life
decisions.reason: The spirit (ruach) may be the proud spirit of rulers or their very breath: God breaks their pride or ends their lives.

decisions.choice: cuts short the breath (B); humbles proud (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of life cut short; Readable gives its plainest result (m2).
